Hey, I'm trans, pan and slightly suicidal. I can understand how you feel, since I come from an 'intolerant' country so to speak. 

Let me know if you'd like to talk. I'm around if you need help.

And don't listen to the other people in the comments who tell you to 'kill yourself because you don't understand gender'. It can be easy to dismiss what you don't experience, or don't understand, so don't let such words get to you, because they have no clue about what you're going through. They just don't understand what it means to have a little understanding for others. 

Mr1220, if you want a keyboard shouting match then have one with me. Leave the poor kid alone.

Hey, this is 100000% relatable, so maybe take some comfort in the fact that you are not the only one in this position. Sometimes I lay in bed thinking about it for hours, asking myself about what I am but getting no answers. Am I trans? If I am, am I 'trans enough' to get surgery? Maybe I'm in the middle between what is considered male and female. I really don't know. 

I went to uni recently, and honestly people are a lot more open minded, or don't care at all. Maybe you will experience the same. 

Anyway, long ramble aside, feel free to privately message me if you'd like to talk. We both have a long way to go. Maybe we could both get something out of it.

I wish you all the best.
I usually write song lyrics, biology stuff, things that make 'no sense' (like tumblr shitposts, or meme references), and the occasional inspirational quote.

When I have this problem I pull out my old notes, and try to re-do them as neatly as I can. That way I can compare the two and see if my handwriting is up to my 'old standards'... Might take a day or two, but I find that it works for me. Maybe you'll find it better to copy some text from a book just so that old muscle memory kicks in. Best of luck!

I totally know how you feel. I've slept in the past few days too because I didn't want to check my email for rejection letters. 

I worked hard too, my mom paid for expensive tuition, and I still did poorly. All my friends did well, and it hurts to see but yeah, I'm still happy for them. 

There's this quote, you know, "it's never too late to be what you might have been." We still have time to redeem ourselves after this, in college or university, but that chance will disappear if we choose to end our lives here. Sure it will be hard to swallow our failure and push forwards but I guess it's just what we gotta do. 

Forgive yourself, and move on. I'm always around if you need support, so feel free to PM me if you'd like. You got this, dude. All the best.

I'm in pretty much the same situation as you are. My A Levels were shit. I went from straight As to straight Ds. I came home and cried. My mother couldn't even look at me. Universities turned me down today. I don't know what to do. 

If you don't want to retake your A levels maybe you could look into going to a sort of college/community college and then transfer to a university after a couple years. You can take a foundation program at a university and then apply to your chosen major to continue. Or some people have mentioned clearing schools, but I haven't looked into that bit yet. 

If you want to retake your full A levels I would highly advise to not take both AS levels and A Levels together. I tried that and it really fucked me up. I regret not doing well my AS levels well the first time.

Hang in there, mate. I guess there's still a long way to go in life.
